source.title: Disentangling trainability and generalization in deep learning
source.authors: Lechao Xiao; Jeffrey Pennington; S. Schoenholz

record.tranche_reason: Reports CIFAR-10 training accuracy across depth and weight-variance configurations, bearing on whether networks train to perfect training accuracy.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-accuracy results for CIFAR-10. Cited results from other studies are not extracted. Other learning-rate and kernel results do not directly test the specified claim versions.
record.test_reason: Finite-width CNN training accuracy tests V1 on a CIFAR-10 subset. Varying initialization variance and depth, together with explicit theoretical learning-rate and convergence results, also tests the initialization-dependent trainability component of V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the phase contrast, but incompletely represents the conclusion. The authors characterize NTK spectral quantities that predict trainability and generalization in wide, deep networks, corroborate these predictions experimentally, and show that trainability can improve while generalization deteriorates. They explicitly restrict their theory's applicability when finite width, large learning rates or changed parameterization break the NTK correspondence.
record.recipe_differences: Finite-width CNN-F trained with SGD on a 1k CIFAR-10 subset; results are presented across weight-variance and depth configurations, rather than the broad benchmark and label conditions in V1.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with phase and depth/weight-variance configuration: perfect training accuracy in the deep chaotic phase, degraded training accuracy in the ordered phase.

fits_no_version.finding: Depth-10 networks become untrainable at sufficiently large learning-rate multipliers in Figure 2(c).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The initial NTK maximum eigenvalue predicts a scale for feasible learning rates; this experiment does not establish above-threshold recovery or curvature dynamics.

fits_no_version.finding: The theoretical continuum residual ReLU model has exponentially growing kernel entries but the same limiting NTK condition number as its plain counterpart; normalization removes the exponential factor.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual connections and normalization can change signal magnitudes without changing asymptotic NTK conditioning in this model.

fits_no_version.finding: Deep chaotic networks fit training examples perfectly while test accuracy remains around 10%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Successful optimization and useful generalization can dissociate in deep networks.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 119, 2020
record.problems: The finite-width experiment uses a 1k subset of CIFAR-10 and reports no model width, numeric training-accuracy values, or uncertainty for the stated phase comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No additional textual training-accuracy results were reported. Figure-only accuracy plots in Figures 2 and 6 were not separately extracted because their values are not stated in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Full CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, width sufficiency, and controlled comparisons of model size, early stopping or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and adding one or two student neurons.
Training-error comparisons of plain batch-normalized CNNs with identity-shortcut counterparts, longer-training controls, and the specified special initialization recipes.

Orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, orthogonal convolution kernels, 10,000-layer training, and direct finite-network training-speed comparisons between activation-matched initialization recipes.
Transient loss increases followed by recovery, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability trajectories, and divergence from initially subthreshold learning rates.
Batch-normalization versus no-normalization training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Explicit theoretical initialization-dependent convergence comparison: ordered-phase learning time grows exponentially with depth, whereas critical initialization has limiting NTK condition number (m+2)/2 for FCN/CNN-F and remains trainable at arbitrary depth in the wide-network analysis. Record the assumptions and learning-rate scaling, rather than treating conditioning alone as measured training accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for any supplied version. Figure-only accuracy results in Figures 2 and 6 are already declared in rows_left_out and are not treated as undeclared omissions. Critical initialization is not necessary for fitting here: chaotic networks also train successfully with appropriately scaled learning rates. No necessity claim about balanced signals is inferred.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, and comparisons with smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes are not tested.
